caption:
Gone are the days when only photographers had access to professional lighting.

For most of the last century, good light was not something you could buy. It was somewhere you had to go. A room with a door, a day rate, and someone else's diary deciding when you were allowed in. The lights alone cost more than the camera. That is why studio portraits looked expensive: because they were.

So two people could stand in the same hotel lobby, wearing the same clothes, with the same face — and one of them went home with a portrait and the other went home with a snapshot. The difference was never talent. It was access.

This photo was taken on a phone, in a lounge, with the lights that happened to be on the ceiling. The second one is the same photo. Nothing was reshot, nothing was restyled, nobody went anywhere. One hard key from camera-right, minimal fill, the background pushed to white — a setup that used to need a studio, a stand and someone to hold it.

Slide 8 is a photo from 2022 taken on an iPhone 13, run through the same tool. Because the point was never that you need better gear. The point is that the door is gone.
